page: Microsoft Azure D32als_v6 is a low-memory variant of the General Purpose Dalv6 series, operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture incorporates 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Supported hardware extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

The configuration provides 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server contains no integrated local storage, requiring external Premium Storage attachments for operating system and data volumes. Hardware acceleration via discrete GPUs is not present, directing all processing tasks to the host CPU cores.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core and compute capabilities, with top-quartile performance in stress-ng single-core tests (3079.55) and Geekbench single-core (2101.0) and multi-core (18099.0) evaluations. PassMark encryption throughput and small model LLM inference also placed in the top 25 percent. Conversely, memory bandwidth for uncached blocks, static web serving throughput, PassMark database operations, and multi-core stress-ng tests placed in the middle 50 percent.

Due to its lower RAM allocation relative to vCPU capacity, the instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for compute-intensive workloads that do not demand extensive memory footprints. Tradeoffs include reliance on networked storage for all disk I/O and potential memory constraints on large datasets. Recommended workloads include software compilation, text and image processing pipelines, batch compute tasks, and API microservices.
description: Microsoft Azure D32als_v6 is a compute-oriented virtual machine from the Dalv6 series, featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 16 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz. Configured with 64.0 GB of memory, the system provides a 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation tailored for processing-dense tasks rather than memory-heavy workloads. The instance includes AVX-512 and advanced cryptographic instruction sets, lacks discrete GPUs, and provides no bundled local disk storage, relying on external Premium Storage. Benchmark testing demonstrates top-quartile single-core performance, multi-core Geekbench scores, cryptographic throughput, and lightweight LLM processing, paired with average memory bandwidth and database execution. This profile makes the instance an efficient choice for software compilation, batch processing, image and text analytics, and compute-bound API services.
